contexts: District general hospital heart failure service
Two nurse prescribers, up to 6 clinic hours per week
Consultant clinics every four to six months
reading: Doses stall because every change waits for a consultant slot, while the retrieved evidence shows that nurse-led titration with fortnightly contact moves doses faster and reduces admissions. The fourth medicine class raises the monitoring load: potassium and kidney function must be checked before changes, which is where the community blood test sites matter. Access is unequal: missed visits cluster in deprived neighbourhoods and among patients far from the hospital, and patients over 80 may need face-to-face visits. Governance rests on the signed-off protocol and the prescribing policy.
